purpose: Permanent, explicitly reviewed code-owned CI governance inputs that extend the legacy monolithic configuration fingerprint baseline without suppressing drift.

entries.reason: Target branch is a read-only identity binding used to reject cross-branch auto-merge registration and is constrained by the verifier to the governed main target.

Expected attestor App ID is a non-secret server-policy identity binding used to fail closed unless exact-candidate readiness is attested by the designated GitHub App; it grants no merge, runtime, provider, database, protected-ref, or Production mutation authority.
Expected base-head SHA is a read-only freshness binding used to reject a finalizer decision if the governed main base moved after candidate construction; it grants no mutation authority.
Expected merge-candidate SHA is a read-only exact-candidate identity binding; any mismatch fails closed before finalizer merge authority can be exercised.
Expected head SHA is a read-only exact-head freshness binding; mismatches fail closed before auto-merge registration.
Expected PR-head SHA is a read-only exact-head binding used to reject stale finalizer evidence when the pull-request source changes; it grants no mutation authority.

Expected status creator ID is a non-secret GitHub identity binding used to reject a required-check status emitted by an unexpected principal; it cannot itself authorize merge or any runtime, provider, database, protected-ref, or Production mutation.

Managed Ruleset name is a non-secret server-policy selector used only to verify the expected main-branch ruleset and its no-bypass protection before finalization; it grants no ruleset mutation or Production authority.
PR number is a read-only identity selector used to bind readiness to one open pull request and inspect blocking labels before registration.
Repository identity is a read-only GitHub API scope binding that prevents readiness evidence from being evaluated against an unintended repository.
Required status-check context is an exact, read-only server-policy readiness input; it does not grant merge, runtime, provider, database, or Production mutation authority.

Required check context is an exact, read-only status identity used by the finalizer verifier; it narrows which App-bound exact-candidate attestation is acceptable and does not grant merge, runtime, provider, database, protected-ref, or Production mutation authority.
GH_TOKEN is a credential reference consumed only for GitHub server-side readback; no credential value is tracked or emitted and the verifier itself performs no merge or protected-ref mutation.

RUNTIME_BASE_URL is consumed by the bounded Migration 1051 metadata-state module only to address the existing admin control read surface; this binding grants no Apply, runtime, database, provider, protected-ref, or Production mutation authority.

EVIDENCE_DIR selects only the ephemeral no-secret evidence directory written by the bounded Migration 1051 metadata-state diagnostic; it grants no runtime, database, provider, protected-ref, or Production mutation authority.

BACKEND_API_KEY is a credential reference consumed only to authenticate the bounded read-only Migration 1051 admin metadata probe. No credential value is tracked or emitted, and this binding cannot grant Apply, runtime, database, provider, protected-ref, or Production mutation authority.

METADATA_DIAGNOSTIC_MODE selects only the bounded metadata-state diagnostic behavior and remains non-authorizing; it does not grant Apply, runtime, database, provider, protected-ref, or Production mutation authority.

Fixed bounded-attempt default for the serialized public exact-SHA policy readiness probes; it is a non-secret code-owned retry invariant and grants no runtime, provider, database, protected-ref, Ruleset Apply, or Production mutation authority.

Fixed bounded retry-delay default for the serialized public exact-SHA policy readiness probes; it is a non-secret code-owned backoff invariant and grants no runtime, provider, database, protected-ref, Ruleset Apply, or Production mutation authority.

Fixed upper bound for Retry-After handling by the public exact-SHA policy readiness probes; it is a non-secret fail-bounded safety invariant and grants no runtime, provider, database, protected-ref, Ruleset Apply, or Production mutation authority.
Static contract identifier for the no-secret GitHub verification report; it is not runtime configuration and grants no signing, repository, provider, database, or Production authority.

RUNTIME_BASE_URL is consumed only by the bounded Migration 1051 VERIFY metadata diagnostic to address the existing admin control read surface; the diagnostic remains read-only and grants no runtime, database, provider, protected-ref, or Production mutation authority.

EVIDENCE_DIR selects only the ephemeral no-secret verification artifact directory for the bounded Migration 1051 metadata diagnostic and does not grant runtime, database, provider, protected-ref, or Production mutation authority.

BACKEND_API_KEY is a credential reference consumed only to authenticate the bounded read-only admin control metadata probe. No credential value is tracked or emitted, and the diagnostic cannot grant Apply, runtime, provider, database, protected-ref, or Production mutation authority.

Exact immutable environment-convergence plan SHA-256 is a non-secret stale-recovery identity binding used by the server-side dry-run evidence and explicit deploy handoff; it is not execution authority by itself and grants no runtime, provider, database, DNS, protected-ref, or Production mutation authority.

Exact non-secret Staging Activation Gateway policy identity propagated between same-run dry-run, binding verification, provider preflight, and deploy steps; it narrows execution to the verified policy and grants no provider, database, DNS, protected-ref, or Production authority.

Expected Staging Activation Gateway policy hash is a non-secret exact-policy identity binding used to fail closed if a stale-recovery dry-run or deploy does not match the governed activation_gateway_staging profile; it grants no provider, database, DNS, protected-ref, or Production mutation authority.

RUNNER_TEMP selects only the ephemeral directory for non-secret stale-recovery dry-run evidence inside the GitHub Actions runner; it is not a runtime target and grants no provider, database, DNS, protected-ref, or Production mutation authority.

Same-run non-secret binding digest joining authoritative convergence plan, exact source identity, policy identity, and Worker bundle before provider access; the digest is verification evidence and is not execution authority.

Exact non-secret main source SHA carried across the Staging Worker refresh workflow to fail closed on source drift and verify artifact provenance; it does not grant provider, database, DNS, protected-ref, or Production mutation authority.

Exact source SHA is a non-secret current-main identity binding for stale-recovery dry-run and deploy verification; the workflow independently proves it equals origin/main before any provider access and this reference alone grants no mutation authority.

Authoritative server-reconstructed convergence-plan digest emitted by the dry-run verifier after exact operator-acknowledgement equality; it is non-secret same-run evidence and the digest itself is explicitly not provider execution authority.

Deterministic non-secret Worker bundle digest bound to the exact source and policy before Cloudflare credentials become visible; it is integrity evidence only and grants no provider, database, DNS, protected-ref, or Production authority.

The gateway policyHashRequired predicate is a code-owned fail-closed policy contract. It only requires attested policy/source evidence for readiness and grants no runtime, database, provider, protected-ref, or Production mutation authority.

The synchronized runtime gateway policyHashRequired predicate is a code-owned fail-closed policy contract and does not grant runtime, database, provider, protected-ref, or Production mutation authority.

The required-default contract validator is a code-owned fail-closed governance predicate for MariaDB SHA2 ordinary-column compatibility; it grants no runtime, database, provider, protected-ref, or Production mutation authority.

The required-default ordering predicate is a code-owned fail-closed governance input that enforces additive DDL placement before omitted-column writers; it grants no runtime, database, provider, protected-ref, or Production mutation authority.

The exact default SQL literal is a code-owned non-secret contract value used to reject wrong sentinel DDL shapes before any disposable replay; it grants no runtime, database, provider, protected-ref, or Production mutation authority.

The required-default SQL evidence literal is a code-owned read-only validator binding for the MariaDB ERROR 1364 contract and cannot authorize runtime, database, provider, protected-ref, or Production mutation.

Fixed lower lifetime bound for signed installer download capabilities; it is a security invariant, contains no secret, and grants no runtime, provider, database, or Production mutation authority.

The Recovery composition factory's configuredComponents readiness label is a non-secret, read-only authority report field. It does not discover providers, contain credentials, or grant runtime, database, protected-ref, or Production mutation authority.

The Recovery readiness allRequiredComponentsConfigured predicate is a non-secret, read-only completeness result for the server-managed authority graph. It cannot enable live execution or grant mutation authority.

The Recovery readiness compositionConfigured predicate is a non-secret, read-only certification result. It reports whether the injected non-live composition is structurally complete and grants no runtime, database, provider, protected-ref, or Production mutation authority.

The Recovery readiness stagingModeValid predicate is a non-secret, read-only environment-bound safety check. It rejects non-staging composition modes and grants no runtime, database, provider, protected-ref, or Production mutation authority.

The Recovery Kernel approvalReservationContext is an internal, sanitized reservation record used to bind one approval claim to one server-issued execution ticket and idempotency key; it contains no credential value and cannot authorize runtime, database, provider, protected-ref, or Production mutation by itself.
The route environment claim is a derived, server-side attestation field used only to reject missing or mismatched Staging identity; it does not accept caller authority or grant mutation.
The requestHost value is derived from the trusted request-host resolver for a fail-closed route boundary; it is not a configurable authority and grants no mutation capability.

The canonical Staging Recovery Admin host is a non-secret route-boundary identity constant. It prevents direct-origin access and grants no runtime, database, provider, protected-ref, or Production mutation authority.

The runtime environment resolver contract identifier is a non-secret code-owned compatibility label for fail-closed identity resolution and grants no runtime, database, provider, protected-ref, or Production mutation authority.

Canonical E2E evidence receives the path of the downloaded disposable MariaDB certification artifact so it can validate and hash that structured evidence. The value is a runner-local file path, contains no secret, and grants no runtime, database, protected-ref, Staging, or Production mutation authority.

Canonical E2E evidence receives the GitHub Actions result of the disposable MariaDB certification job to fail closed when certification fails or is cancelled. This is non-secret CI status metadata and grants no runtime, database, protected-ref, Staging, or Production mutation authority.

Upper bound for the repository-owned E2E child-test timeout. It is a non-secret fail-closed CI governance constant that prevents unbounded or excessively long child execution and grants no runtime, provider, database, protected-ref, or Production mutation authority.

Lower bound for the repository-owned E2E child-test timeout. It is a non-secret fail-closed CI governance constant that prevents an unsafe near-zero timeout from weakening test execution and grants no runtime, provider, database, protected-ref, or Production mutation authority.
configuredSurfaceKeys is a derived registry selection used to generate environment-specific OpenAPI projections. It is not a credential or live activation switch and grants no mutation authority.

existingPolicy is a read-only snapshot of the previously generated Activation Gateway policy used solely to preserve provenance hashes when Gateway semantic content is unchanged. It contains no credential, does not select a live provider or target, grants no runtime mutation authority, and cannot activate Production.
Readiness failure path points only to the downloaded exact-run artifact in the ephemeral Actions workspace and is used for bounded read-only diagnostic publication.

Source conclusion is an exact read-only workflow-run fact used to select success-marker or bounded failure-diagnostic publication; it grants no Apply, runtime, provider, database, protected-ref, or Production mutation authority.
Readiness state path points only to the downloaded exact-run artifact in the ephemeral Actions workspace and is read for bounded stage metadata without runtime mutation.

Existing server-issued backend authentication is read from the bounded Staging environment only to verify the exact role-bundle binding before local execution; no secret value is stored and this entry grants no database, provider, or Production authority.

Staging Recovery verification endpoint selection is constrained in code to activation-dev.mad4b.com and is used only for exact ticket role-bundle verification; it grants no database, provider, or Production authority.

Process-local sentinel passed by the verified wrapper after server validation of exact ticket role-bundle bindings; it is not caller authority, contains no secret, and grants no Production or provider authority.

Disposable MariaDB certification uses a fixed non-secret batch claim token only inside its isolated CI database to prove that a poller reads back exactly the rows atomically claimed by its own token. It is test-fixture data, not runtime configuration or credential material, and grants no Staging, Production, provider, or external database authority.

Disposable MariaDB certification is intentionally pinned to the GitHub Actions service port 3306. This is a non-secret CI-only loopback invariant; the certifier separately refuses non-local DB_HOST values and grants no Staging, Production, provider, or external database authority.

The default baseline-extension path is the code-owned locator for the permanent configuration governance extension authority. It selects a tracked report-only contract, contains no credential, and grants no runtime, database, protected-ref, or Production mutation authority.

The OpenAPI detail-batch output path is a code-owned allowlist binding for the registered frontend generated-artifact writer; it limits writes to one governed tracked artifact and grants no runtime, database, provider, protected-ref, or Production mutation authority.

The platform configuration entry guard default extension path is a tracked, read-only governance locator used to recognize explicitly reviewed CI inputs; it contains no credential and grants no runtime, database, provider, protected-ref, or Production mutation authority.

The enrollment CLI reads the non-secret broker key ID used to address an exact server-owned HMAC credential; the secret value remains outside the repository and this reference grants no runtime or Production authority.
The enrollment CLI reads the canonical non-secret Site origin to construct and validate the exact broker binding; it performs no network request, broker mutation, or Production activation.

The enrollment CLI reads the canonical non-secret Site Profile UUID solely to bind the planned broker credential to one exact site; it grants no runtime, database, provider, or Production mutation authority.
